question: For root bracket 1 and the two punctured real lambda boxes, can the Q0-normalized declared Gamma_1 quotient functional and its local lambda derivative be enclosed after a finite cutoff plus analytic rotating-frame tail?
primary_sources: NIST DLMF, modified-Bessel and Wronskian conventions: https://dlmf.nist.gov/10

declared_conventions.reference_equation: c_p,QQ=A_0*c_p; c_p(-4)=1 and c_p,Q(-4)=0; c_p is lambda-independent
declared_conventions.projective_normalization: U=u/u(Q0), Z=partial_lambda U, so U(Q0)=1, U_Q(Q0)=r=-rho(Q0)-x0-1/2, Z(Q0)=0 and Z_Q(Q0)=-s(Q0)
declared_conventions.execution: SymPy exact identities and python-flint Arb interval Taylor with analytic rotating-frame tail bounds; no black-box ODE, quadrature, root solve, finite difference or sampling

method_reuse.role: exact-rational parsing, outward interval primitives, coefficient-derivative and whole-step-majorant semantics only; no old result is evidence

upstream_results.role: provides root-1 Q0-normalized rho and local projective sensitivity intersections
pins the selected lambda-independent c_p reference and declared Gamma_1 Wronskian convention

assumptions: Every interval statement is uniform only on root bracket 1 and one displayed lambda box at a time; root uniqueness is not assumed.
The Q0 result supplies projective data only. The U(Q0)=1 normalization defines a quotient functional, not an absolute actual Gamma_1 amplitude.
The finite cutoff Taylor system is enlarged by a whole-step D13 bound on full parameter boxes. The omitted half-line is bounded analytically in rotating norms.
The lambda-zero row is a regression of the declared normalized derivative convention; no nonzero-lambda continuation through lambda=0 is inferred.
